assumptions_and_reasoning.aggregation_existence: Horizontal aggregation is performed at common prices with truncation and correspondence choices retained. Continuity plus opposite excess-demand signs supports existence; strict decrease gives uniqueness. Zero trade can have an interval of supporting prices. The implicit comparative-static derivative has the correct sign under strict downward demand/upward supply, and is distinguished from dynamic convergence or identification.
assumptions_and_reasoning.welfare: Quasilinear preferences, unit numeraire and a nonbinding numeraire constraint/unrestricted transfer premise are stated before exact money surplus. Concave benefits, convex variable costs and efficient buyer/producer allocation support the inverse curves. CS/PS are not revenue, and committed fixed cost separates PS from profit. Startup-fee integration is explicitly qualified. Transaction payments and tax revenue cancel exactly once. The chapter distinguishes unweighted gains, actual Pareto improvements, feasible compensation, weighted social objectives and omitted externalities.
assumptions_and_reasoning.tax_domains: Differentiating D(ps+t)=S(ps) gives dpb/dt=S'/(S'-D'), dps/dt=D'/(S'-D') and dQ/dt=D'S'/(S'-D'). The common price/quantity normalization for elasticity shares is restricted to an initially untaxed equilibrium. Nonlinear finite taxes and preexisting wedges are correctly separated from that local rule. The finite triangle holds for the stated linear inverse curves only within the positive-trade domain; at or above the 24-unit choke wedge in the example, output is truncated at zero. Legal remittance invariance is tied to the same incentives, compliance/base and transaction/enforcement conditions. Limiting perfectly elastic/inelastic cases are handled with feasibility qualifications.
assumptions_and_reasoning.entry: Global minimum average cost, smooth interior p=MC and zero profit are distinguished from a stationary-point test. Identical technologies, constant industry input prices, avoidable long-run cost and divisible entry support the ideal horizontal relation. The chapter correctly distinguishes this industry result from constant returns of a single firm at all outputs. The 15.5-firm calculation is not rounded into a claimed long-run equilibrium; the 15/16-firm conditional configurations demonstrate the different price/profit incentives and explicitly require a separate finite entry model.
assumptions_and_reasoning.rationing: A ceiling specifies intended demands/supplies but not the buyer allocation. Highest-value allocation supports the ordinary area to actual Q. The exercise explicitly changes to a continuum of one-unit buyers and an equal-service-probability lottery; that additional specification identifies expected benefit. Quantity loss and misallocation loss are kept distinct, with no fabricated queueing or administrative cost.
assumptions_and_reasoning.instruction_scope: Every required method is introduced before the exercises, and both determinate and open-ended solution criteria are supplied. Units are per-week quantity and dollar totals versus per-unit prices/tax. Price-taking is stated as an assumption. The identification critique requires actual relevance/exogeneity/exclusion or a scoped randomized design rather than naming an instrument. The general-equilibrium successor remains explicitly planned.

independent_calculations.method: Used a fresh ephemeral standard-library Fraction calculation, with two-equation determinant solutions for buyer/seller prices and price/per-firm quantity. Integrated individual buyer groups' marginal benefits and producer groups' marginal costs, rather than copying the checker’s aggregate triangle ledger. Integrated the lottery over reservation-value density instead of quantity rank. No new program or data file was written.
